analysis.summary: In this round, 13 of 30 members bought the 328 HKD member fare, all within their stated base-fare budgets; 12 of these also accepted the 410 HKD regular fare as fallback. The other 17 declined: 12 cited no available ticket within budget, 3 cited route/date mismatch, and 2 cited unconfirmed companions. No inventory denials occurred and quota was not binding. Declines are stated reasons, not measured willingness to pay, and observed intentions are not fulfilled purchases.
analysis.hypothesis: Among members whose stated base-fare budget falls between 328 and 410 HKD, offering the 328 HKD member fare yields higher stated purchase intention than offering only the 410 HKD regular fare; this can be tested by randomizing which fare is shown.

analysis.summary: In this round, 18 of 28 members stated an intention to buy the member fare at HKD 244.35, all citing it as within their base-fare budget; 10 declined. Of the declines, 5 cited no ticket both available and within budget, 3 cited route/date mismatch, and 2 cited unconfirmed companions. No inventory denials occurred and quota was not binding. All purchases were member-fare intents; no regular-fare purchases. Reasons are stated explanations, not measured willingness to pay, and intentions are not fulfilled purchases.
analysis.hypothesis: Raising the member fare above HKD 244.35 will reduce stated member-fare purchase intentions among members whose base-fare budgets sit just above 244.35, while members with budgets well above it will remain buyers.

analysis.summary: In this round, 18 of 28 members intended to buy the member fare at HKD 244.35, all citing it as within their base-fare budget; 10 declined. Of the declines, 5 cited no ticket both available and within budget, 3 cited route/date mismatch, and 2 cited unconfirmed companions. No inventory denials occurred and quota was not binding. All purchases were member-fare intents; no regular-fare purchases. Declines reflect budget, schedule, or companion constraints rather than a single price objection.
analysis.hypothesis: Among members whose base-fare budget is below HKD 410 but at or above HKD 244.35, member-fare conversion stays high; those declining cite budget below HKD 244.35 or schedule/companion mismatch. Testing a slightly higher member fare would reveal whether budget-constrained members near the threshold switch to decline.

analysis.summary: In this synthetic round, 18 of 28 members stated intent to buy the member fare at HKD 244.35, all citing it as within their base-fare budget; 10 declined. Declines split between budget/availability mismatch (5), route or date mismatch (3), and companions unable to confirm (2). No inventory denials occurred and quota was not binding. All purchases are stated intentions, not fulfilled purchases. Reasons are explanations, not measured willingness to pay, and are not independent samples.
analysis.hypothesis: Raising the member fare above HKD 244.35 will reduce stated member purchase intent, with the largest drop among members whose base-fare budget is near or below HKD 300, while high-budget members retain regular-fare fallback.

analysis.summary: In this round, 18 of 28 members chose the member fare of HKD 244.35, all within their stated base-fare budgets; 10 declined. Among decliners, several cited no ticket both available and within budget, three cited route/date mismatch, and two cited unconfirmed companions. No inventory denials occurred and quota was not binding. All purchases are stated intentions, not confirmed fulfilled purchases. Price objections cannot be cleanly separated from availability or route/date mismatch for the budget-citing decliners.
analysis.hypothesis: At a member fare of HKD 244.35, members whose stated base-fare budget is below HKD 410 will still buy the member fare but decline the regular fallback; raising the member fare toward HKD 410 should reduce member purchases among this low-budget subgroup more than among higher-budget members.

analysis.summary: In round 10 at a member fare of HKD 244.35, 18 of 28 members chose BUY_MEMBER (observed intentions, not fulfilled purchases); no regular-fare buyers. All buyers cited the member fare fitting their base-fare budget and matching date/route. Declines split between budget/availability constraints and route/date mismatch or unconfirmed companions. Member quota was not binding. Reasons are stated explanations, not measured willingness to pay, and do not constitute independent samples.
analysis.hypothesis: At member fares above HKD 244.35, members whose base-fare budget sits just above 244.35 (e.g. 244.75-284.31) will decline more often than higher-budget members, indicating a price-response threshold near their stated budgets.
